short_description: A warm first phone agreement you write together, plus a readiness checklist, phone-free zones and 30 phone-free afternoons. Ages 9–12. Fillable, Letter + A4.
long_description:
A first phone is a big step toward independence. This printable kit helps you take it together, calmly, with plenty of play along the way.

Start with “Are we ready?”, a 16-point checklist with no score and no right age, plus 10 real-world practice missions like an alarm-clock week and learning two phone numbers by heart. Then write Our First Phone Agreement: tick from 18 kid promises and 8 grown-up promises, add your own, and sign it. It is a warm agreement, not a contract of punishments. The phone is never a prize and never a punishment; when something goes wrong, you pause, talk it through and adjust.

Choose your phone-free zones and times (grown-ups too), post the 8 zone signs, and fill in one Fridge-Door Tech Plan for the whole house. Then try 30 Phone-Free Afternoons: build, ride, cook, invent and explore. 26 of the 30 ideas need nothing to buy, each has a 2-minute easier version, a harder one and a safety line, and a certificate waits at day 30.

Includes a 2-page grown-up guide, a monthly check-in, quick answers, 3 colorways and a low-ink file. Every blank line and tick box is fillable in a free PDF reader; printed words, colors and pictures can’t be changed. US Letter and A4.

Never names an app, a phone brand or a company. Parent education, not medical or professional advice. Every afternoon idea follows our published safety rules. Digital download: nothing is shipped. For personal and family use.

compliance_notes: Rule 1: no health, medical, mental-health, sleep, brain, grades or safety-outcome claims anywhere; the guide, quick answers, START HERE and listing say it is parent education, not medical or professional advice, and point health questions to the child's doctor. No autism, ADHD, therapy or diagnosis words in the product, images, keywords or tags (Autism searches rule). Rule 2 and the spec: no app, website, device brand or company is named anywhere; the phone is drawn as a generic rounded rectangle with a face (no buttons, notch or logos); fillable instructions say 'a free PDF reader that supports forms' rather than naming a reader. Rule 4 child safety: every one of the 30 afternoon ideas carries its own safety line (helmets, grown-up knows route and return time, grown-up handles knives/stove/craft knives, draped never tied and no cords near necks, look don't taste, no berries or mushrooms, never look at the sun, marbles, beads and small pieces away from under-3s, no nuts, popcorn or whole grapes for toddlers who join a snack or picnic, 'a grown-up is home and nearby' where no specific hazard applies); the challenge page adds a 'Safe afternoons, every time' card; the 'Ask in person' mission keeps a grown-up close by; no balloons, cords or choking-hazard foods; sign pages say the grown-up keeps scissors and pieces away from children under 3. Listing wording: 'Every afternoon idea follows our published safety rules' (never 'safety-checked'). Rule 5: no research citations are used. Rule 7 / ORIGINALITY.md: the spec's 'Family Tech Plan' is renamed 'Our Fridge-Door Tech Plan' because 'Family ___ Plan' names are retired (they echo a free AAP plan); no 'Screen-Smart', 'Reset', 'detox' or 'Wait Until' wording; the Etsy edition points buyers to 'your Purchases page' without naming the marketplace, per the spec's never-name-a-company rule; the nightcap motif is our own (The Day the Tablet Slept). The phrase 'contract' appears only in Etsy tags/keywords because buyers search for it; the product copy says plainly that it is 'a warm agreement, not a contract of punishments'. faq.a: 40 activities and 10 tools: a 16-point readiness checklist, 10 practice missions, Our First Phone Agreement (18 kid and 8 grown-up promises to choose from, plus a write-your-own page), phone-free zones and times, 8 zone signs, a Fridge-Door Tech Plan (example + blank), the 30 Phone-Free Afternoons challenge with tracker and certificate, and a monthly check-in.
Written for ages 9–12. There's no right age for a first phone; every family decides. No phone yet? Start with the checklist, missions and 30 afternoons.
About 5 minutes to print. Filling in the agreement and plan together takes about 30 minutes, then 5 minutes a month to check in. Nothing needs cutting unless you want the signs.

Instant download: nothing is shipped. On Etsy your files stay on your Purchases page; on our site the link is in your order email. On a phone, open the link in a web browser and save each PDF to your files first.

Every blank line and tick box is fillable in a free PDF reader that supports forms: names, dates, times, promises, zones, the yes-list, plan answers, the tracker and the certificate. Printed wording, colors and pictures can't be changed.

faq.q: Can I give it as a gift?
faq.a: Yes. Buy it and forward the download email, or print the pages for the family. The personal license then belongs to that family. [VERIFY that each store can send a download straight to a gift recipient.]

faq.q: Is there a printed or boxed version?
faq.a: Not yet. A write-in paperback workbook may follow on Amazon (see the listing); we'll say so here when it exists.

faq.q: Can grandparents or a second home use our copy?
faq.a: Yes. The personal license covers your own family's homes, including grandparents and sitters who care for your child.

faq.q: Can our PTA, class, library or program use it?
faq.a: Not with this license: it covers one family. Each family can buy its own copy. Group and program licenses aren't offered yet.

Not yet: the printed text is in English. Every fillable field accepts Spanish or any language, so you can write your promises in the language you know best. A Spanish edition would be made by a human translator, never by machine.

faq.q: What if my child tells me something worrying?
faq.a: Thank them for telling and stay calm. Don't reply or delete anything yet; save a copy so you can look at it together, then talk it through. If someone may be at risk right now, call your local emergency number. (This answer is also on the quick-answers page.)

faq.q: Does it name apps or phone brands?
faq.a: No. It works with any phone, tablet or console. The yes-list lets your family write in the apps, games and groups you've agreed on.

faq.q: Is this medical or professional advice?
faq.a: No. It's parent education and family planning. For questions about your child's health or development, talk with your child's doctor.
Digital downloads follow the shop's published refund policy. If a file won't open or print, we fix it or send it again [link the policy page at launch].
